panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Real patient MRI showing basilar invagination in the reported Klippel-Feil syndrome case, with the red arrow indicating the offending dens and severe cord compression. B: Real patient MRI demonstrating the target disease-associated basilar invagination and marked cervicomedullary compression. C: Patient axial MRI at C1 showing the craniovertebral abnormality responsible for severe cord compression in the Klippel-Feil case. D: Patient axial MRI at C1-2 showing the target disease-associated basilar invagination with severe cord compression. E: Patient axial MRI from the complete preoperative series documenting the craniovertebral abnormality associated with the Klippel-Feil case. F: Patient axial MRI from the complete preoperative series associated with basilar invagination in the reported Klippel-Feil syndrome case.

panels.figure_caption: Preoperative MR imaging, (A) T1 weighted mid-sagittal MR imaging, (B) T2 weighted mid-sagittal MR imaging, (C) T2 weighted axial MR imaging at C1, (D) T2 weighted axial MR imaging at C1-2, (E) T2 weighted axial MR imaging at C2, (F) T2 weighted axial MR imaging at C3. The spinal cord was compressed severely due to basilar invagination. The red arrows show severe compression of the cervicomedullary cord by the dens.
in_text_mentions: Preoperative cervical radiographs revealed a short neck and a C2/3 fusion anomaly. Dens protrusion into the foramen magnum measured 9.4 mm above McGregor’s line and 4.2 mm above McRae’s line, with an anteroposterior (AP) diameter of the foramen magnum measuring 10.7 mm (Figure 2). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) depicted severe compression of the cervicomedullary cord by the dens, with a cervicomedullary angle (CMA) measuring 116 degrees (Figure 3).
